result:
I could not derive the value of t independently, and none of the three answers passes the one sanity check I could run, so my choice is a weak guess.

**Check with h = 1.** The case h = 1 reduces to point sets in PG(3,q) with at most t points on any plane and size (t−2)q + t. Taking t = q+1 gives q² + 1 points, which is an ovoid, and ovoids exist for q > 2. So a correct formula should plausibly give q+1 at h = 1.

**Solution 1 (t = q−1).** At h = 1 this gives q−1, not q+1. It also has no dependence on h, although the problem asks for a function of q and h.

**Solution 2 (t = q^h − 1).** At h = 1 this gives q−1, so it also fails the check. Its justification is only a vague appeal to "the largest power of q minus 1".

**Solution 3 (t = q^{2h}).** At h = 1 this gives q², which is far too large. Its claimed k = 3 case (t = q^h) also fails at h = 1, since the hyperoval case has t = 2. Its "general pattern" q^{(k−2)h} looks invented.

Since all three fail the check, I am picking the one that at least depends on both q and h and is of a plausible size. That is Solution 2.

CHOICE: 2
